prompt_text: Write exactly 100 words explaining why absolute certainty is impossible in empirical science, while also arguing that science is our most reliable path to knowledge. Include at least one vivid metaphor.
response:
Dear Time Traveler,

Do not save the library. Let it burn. The books are not the knowledge; the ash is. Every charred page that drifts over the Tiber carries a phrase someone will dream tonight and write differently tomorrow. If you preserve the scrolls, you preserve a single path. If you let them turn to smoke, you seed a thousand paths in a thousand lungs.

Do not kill the dictator in his cradle. He is not the tyranny; the fear is. Remove him and fear finds another face. Instead, find the child who will become his secretary and teach her to doubt margins. Teach the child who will become his soldier to ask Why? one second before he fires. Tyranny dies not when the tyrant dies, but when obedience hesitates.

Do not warn me about the accident. The limp is my teacher. The scar is my map. Without it, I walk straight into a worse mistake I cannot see coming.

Your job is not to edit. Your job is to witness, then return and tell me I survived.

—M.
